title: 18S-V4 rRNA amplification from total genomic DNA for NGS Illumina sequencing
author: Estelle Bigeard
materials: Gel electrophoresis apparatus (tray, comb, cuve, power source)
PCR purification kit (e.g., NucleoSpin Gel and PCR Clean-up Kit)

PCR products should be checked initially by gel electrophoresis for unspecific amplification and band size. - Check PCR products on agarose gel to see if the bands are weak or strong. Prepare an agarose gel 1-1.5% in 0.5X TAE buffer Microwave until the solution is clear (2 minutes) Stain with 20 µL ethidium bromide per 100ml (or SYBR-safe dye) Ethidium bromide 10 mg/ml Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #E1510 Be careful : Put labcoat, nitriles gloves! Prepare tray & comb(s) Pour gel into tray When the gel is polymerized, remove comb Load gel in electrophesis cuve containing the same 0.5X TAE buffer Gel must be covered Cut one strip of parafilm. Load 1-2 µL loading dye onto parafilm, one drop per sample Mix 1 to 3 μl of each PCR product with loading dye (up & down 3 times) Load it in the agarose gel Load 3 µL of SmartLadder into first and/or last well Close & Plug in electrodes to power source Run the migration for ~120 V, 30-45 minutes Observe results using a UV imager like Image Quant LAZ4000, Ge Healthcare The negative control must be negative and the positive control must be positive to validate the PCR. The size of amplicons is indicated in Table 1 and 2. - Samples with failed PCRs (or spurious bands) are re-amplified by optimizing the PCR (further template dilution to 1:100 or using BSA/other additives) to produce correct bands, or purified using a purification kit like “Nuclesopin Gel & Clean up kit– Macherey-Nagel”. Amplicons are stored at -20°C until treatment.

steps.title: Extract and quantify nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Extract DNA (or RNA‑then‑cDNA) from each sample with an appropriate kit, then measure concentration and purity using NanoDrop or Qubit/PicoGreen; accept A260/280 ≥ 1.8 and a DNA concentration of at least 1 ng/µL (aim for 5 ng/µL for PCR).

substeps.instruction: Use a method/kit suited to the sample type (environmental filtrate, sorted cells, etc.).
If starting from RNA, reverse‑transcribe to cDNA before proceeding.
Quantify each extract; record A260/280 and concentration.
If concentration is below 5 ng/µL, keep the sample as‑is (no further normalization).
Optionally run a 0.8 % agarose gel (1 µL sample + loading buffer) to check integrity; detection limit ≈10 ng.

steps.title: Prepare primer stock and working solutions
steps.instruction: Reconstitute Illumina‑tailed primers (TAReuk454FWD1 and TAReukREV3_modified or V4R_Zig) at 100 µM in TE (100 µM TE stock) and dilute 1:10 to a 10 µM working solution; store all stocks and working aliquots at –20 °C, preparing them in a PCR HEPA‑filter hood with molecular‑grade water.

substeps.instruction: Order primers from EUROGENTEC with RP‑HPLC purification, 10 or 40 nmol scale, supplied at 100 µM in TE.
Dilute 10 µL of 100 µM stock into 90 µL TE to obtain 10 µM working solution.
Aliquot and keep both stock and working solutions at –20 °C.

steps.title: Pilot PCR test with non‑tailed primers
steps.instruction: Select a few representative samples and run low‑cycle PCRs using the same V4 primers without the Illumina tail (ordered with standard Se‑POP purification) to determine the optimal DNA input amount and verify amplification before library preparation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR mixes as described in step 4 but using non‑tailed primers.
Run a small number of cycles (low cycle number) and assess products on a gel.
Choose the DNA amount that gives a clear ~380 bp band for the full batch.

steps.title: Set up triplicate PCR reactions
steps.instruction: In a UV‑sterilized area, assemble three 20 µL PCRs per sample using Phusion® High‑Fidelity PCR Master Mix (high GC template) with the Illumina‑tailed primers, adding the DNA amount determined in step 3 (typically 5 ng per reaction); include one negative control per plate and, if desired, a positive mock community control.

substeps.instruction: Label plates/tubes and add nuclease‑free water.
For each 20 µL reaction: add Phusion Master Mix, 10 µM forward primer, 10 µM reverse primer, and the calculated volume of DNA template.
Prepare a no‑template negative control with water instead of DNA.
Optionally add a mock‑community DNA as a positive control.

steps.title: Run PCR thermal cycling
steps.instruction: Place the PCR plate in a thermocycler and run the program listed in Table 5 (high initial denaturation, low number of cycles, appropriate annealing/extension times) using the Phusion® Master Mix conditions.

steps.title: Verify PCR products by agarose gel
steps.instruction: Load 1 µL of each PCR product with loading buffer onto a 0.8 % agarose gel, run, and confirm the presence of a single ~380 bp band; the gel image will later be sent to the sequencing platform for QC.

steps.title: Pool and clean PCR amplicons
steps.instruction: Combine the three replicates for each sample, then purify the pooled product with the Macherey‑Nagel NucleoSpin™ Gel and PCR Clean‑up Kit using the modified elution protocol.

substeps.instruction: Add the pooled PCR to the spin column.
First elution: add 30 µL TE pre‑heated to 70 °C, incubate 5 min, centrifuge 11 000 g for 1 min.
Second elution: add another 30 µL pre‑heated TE (or the first eluate), centrifuge 11 000 g for 1 min.
Aliquot 2.5 µL of the final eluate for downstream quantification.
Store purified amplicons at –20 °C.

steps.title: Quantify purified amplicons
steps.instruction: Measure the concentration and purity (260/280 and 260/230 ratios) of each purified PCR product using a Nanoquant Plate on the Spark Tecan instrument (2 µL per well) or, alternatively, a Qubit 4 fluorometer.

steps.title: Prepare libraries and submit for sequencing
steps.instruction: Take a picture of the agarose gel to verify band quality, organize the purified PCR plates for shipment, freeze them on dry ice, and send them to the sequencing platform; follow the platform‑specific library‑preparation protocol (e.g., Illumina MiSeq 2 × 250 bp, Genomer Platform protocols).

substeps.instruction: Capture gel images showing purity, degradation, and band intensity.
Arrange PCR plates in appropriate containers for dry‑ice shipment.
Include the gel picture and any required metadata with the shipment.
Adhere to the sequencing centre’s library‑prep instructions (e.g., protocols.io “Preparation of libraries (Metabarcoding) for Illumina sequencing – Genomer Platform”).
